chief_complaint: abdominal obesity, moon face, purple striae, and muscle weakness
hpi_details: A 44-year-old female presents to the clinic with abdominal obesity, moon face, purple striae, and muscle weakness. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks her rapid weight gain and rounded face are just early menopause combined with severe work stress.
concerns: She is worried that her profound leg weakness means she will soon be unable to climb the stairs at work and keep her job.
expectations: She hopes to get blood tests to check her hormones and find out why these purple stretch marks keep spreading.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Cushing Syndrome is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Initial evaluation requires biochemical confirmation with accepted screening tests such as late-night salivary cortisol, 24-hour urinary free cortisol, or low-dose dexamethasone suppression; ACTH measurement and directed imaging follow only after hypercortisolism is confirmed.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: abdominal obesity, moon face, purple striae, and muscle weakness

Key HPI features: A 44-year-old female presents to the clinic with abdominal obesity, moon face, purple striae, and muscle weakness. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Cushing Syndrome.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Cushing Syndrome.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Simple obesity without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.

Ignoring critical warning signs such as: severe hypertension, hypokalaemia, rapidly progressive new-onset diabetes, rapid onset of symptoms over weeks rather than months, signs of adrenal crisis (hypotension, severe weakness, or vomiting) if steroids are withdrawn abruptly.
management_principles: Confirm hypercortisolism with appropriate screening tests, then measure ACTH and obtain directed pituitary or adrenal imaging only after biochemical confirmation
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Cushing Syndrome
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Cushing Syndrome
Implement evidence-based management plan: Confirm hypercortisolism biochemically, then use ACTH-directed imaging to determine the source

teaching.one_liner: Excess cortisol causing abdominal obesity, moon face, purple striae, and muscle weakness.
red_flags: Severe hypertension, hypokalaemia, or rapidly progressive new-onset diabetes — suggests ectopic ACTH secretion (e.g., small cell lung cancer) rather than a pituitary adenoma
Rapid onset of symptoms over weeks rather than months — raises concern for an adrenal or ectopic malignancy
Signs of adrenal crisis (hypotension, severe weakness, vomiting) if steroids are withdrawn abruptly — a medical emergency

must_ask.say: Where is the weight gain concentrated?

history.answer: My belly has been getting really big and round, and my face looks swollen and puffy like a full moon.
It started about three to four months ago and has been creeping up on me slowly.
Everything has been steadily getting worse over the past few weeks, especially the belly weight and facial puffiness.
The weight has collected right around my stomach and the back of my neck, while my arms and legs actually look thinner.
My cheeks look puffy, round, and flushed red, so friends have been asking me why my face looks so swollen.
My thighs and upper arms feel very weak, making it hard to climb stairs or get up from a low chair.
I noticed these wide, dark reddish-purple stretch marks across my belly and hips a few weeks ago.
My skin feels paper-thin, and I get large black-and-blue bruises from the slightest bump.
I feel completely exhausted and drained by midday, no matter how much rest I get.
Nothing seems to make it better, and climbing stairs or standing up makes the muscle weakness much more obvious.
I have gained about eight kilograms over four months, even though I have not been eating any more than usual.
No, I have never taken steroid pills, used steroid creams, or received steroid joint injections.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or night sweats.
No, I do not have headaches, blurry vision, or loss of side vision.
No, I have not had any severe dizziness, fainting spells, or intractable nausea and vomiting.
No, I have never experienced anything like this before.
I tried cutting down my calories and walking every evening, but I could not lose any weight and my legs just felt too weak.
I struggle to get up from my desk at work and feel very self-conscious about my changed facial appearance.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 142/90 mmHg, heart rate is 76 beats per minute, respiratory rate is 16 breaths per minute, body temperature is 36.6 degrees Celsius, and oxygen saturation is 99% on room air.
Rounded moon facies with facial plethora, prominent central adiposity, and a prominent dorsocervical fat pad.
Multiple wide violaceous striae across the lower abdomen and flanks, skin thinning, and several scattered ecchymoses on the forearms without active bleeding.
Distended, obese abdomen with prominent purple striae wider than one centimeter, without surgical scars.
Soft and non-tender throughout with excess subcutaneous adiposity; no palpable hepatosplenomegaly or abdominal mass.
Bilateral proximal muscle weakness in the hip flexors and shoulder abductors (grade 4/5), while distal motor strength is fully preserved (5/5).
Visual fields are intact to confrontation testing with normal extraocular movements and no bitemporal visual field cuts.
Trace symmetric pitting edema over both lower shins without erythema or calf tenderness.
Biceps, triceps, patellar, and Achilles deep tendon reflexes are 2+ bilaterally, and plantar responses are flexor.
